title: Using Intraday Information Combinations for Optimal Futures Hedging
abstract: Intraday-based volatility estimators have been shown to provide a better estimation for actual return volatility than the one using daily squared returns. This study proposes a new class of multivariate BEKK models by adding combinations of intraday-based realized volatility (RV) and realized range (RR) estimators at the right-hand side of daily-return-based BEKK model for a forecasting purpose. The optimal combinations of using intraday information are discussed by evaluating them in a context of a futures hedge. Using daily data on S&P 500 index and futures, it is found that hedging models with intraday information can provide better out-of-sample hedging performance than the model using only daily returns. Particularly, as the information used by investors increases, the out-of-sample hedging performance generally improves. Hence, it is suggested that investors should exploit intraday data in decisions when the finer information are available for volatility estimation.
